name: Sensitive data sent to external model provider
description: A data flow carrying confidential or restricted data targets a hosted model API, risking data exposure to a third party.
recommendation: Classify data before sending to external model providers. Apply data masking, use private endpoints, or switch to self-hosted models for sensitive workloads.

name: AI agent or tool connector without approval flow
description: An AI agent or tool connector does not have a human-in-the-loop approval flow configured, allowing autonomous consequential actions.
recommendation: Configure human-in-the-loop approval for high-impact actions. Implement approval workflows for data modifications, external calls, and financial operations.

name: AI agent or tool connector without RBAC
description: An AI agent or tool connector lacks role-based access control, potentially allowing excessive permissions.
recommendation: Implement RBAC on all AI agent tool connectors. Apply least-privilege principles and scope permissions to only the resources and actions required.

name: Public-facing prompt input without guardrails
description: A prompt input component is internet-facing but has no input validation or guardrail configured, leaving it vulnerable to prompt injection.
recommendation: Deploy input validation and guardrails on all public-facing prompt inputs. Implement prompt injection detection, input sanitization, and content policy enforcement.

name: Public-facing prompt input without moderation
description: A prompt input component is internet-facing but no moderation layer is present in the data flow path to the model.
recommendation: Add a moderation layer or content safety filter between public prompt inputs and the LLM to catch harmful or adversarial inputs.

name: Fine-tuning pipeline with external or untrusted data
description: A fine-tuning pipeline consumes data from an external dataset source without apparent validation controls, risking training data poisoning.
recommendation: Validate all training data sources for integrity and provenance. Implement data pipeline validation, anomaly detection, and review processes for fine-tuning datasets.

name: Vector database accessible from public boundary
description: A vector database is included in a public-internet trust boundary or lacks access controls, risking unauthorized access to indexed documents and embeddings.
recommendation: Ensure vector databases are not directly internet-facing. Place behind API gateways with authentication and RBAC. Restrict access to authorized RAG pipelines only.

name: Model outputs triggering actions without human review
description: A data flow from an LLM or AI agent directly triggers a tool connector or backend service action without a human-in-the-loop or approval step in between.
recommendation: Add human-in-the-loop review for consequential actions triggered by model outputs. Implement approval workflows for write operations and external interactions.

name: Unencrypted data flow crossing trust boundary
description: A data flow that crosses a trust boundary is not encrypted, exposing data to interception.
recommendation: Encrypt all data flows crossing trust boundaries using TLS 1.2+ or higher. Use mutual TLS for service-to-service communication across boundary lines.

name: Unauthenticated data flow crossing trust boundary
description: A data flow crossing a trust boundary does not require authentication, allowing unauthorized access.
recommendation: Require authentication on all data flows that cross trust boundaries. Use API keys, OAuth tokens, or mutual TLS certificates.

name: Credentials in unencrypted data flow
description: A data flow carrying credentials is not encrypted, exposing sensitive authentication data.
recommendation: Immediately encrypt all data flows carrying credentials. Use TLS 1.2+ and consider additional encryption layers for credential transport.

name: Training data from external source without validation
description: A training data repository or dataset source is marked as external but lacks input validation controls, risking data poisoning.
recommendation: Validate all external training data sources. Implement data quality checks, provenance verification, and anomaly scanning before use in training pipelines.

name: AI component without logging or monitoring
description: An AI component (LLM, agent, inference pipeline) does not have logging enabled, preventing detection of misuse or anomalous behavior.
recommendation: Enable logging and monitoring on all AI components. Log prompts, outputs, latency, error rates, and unusual query patterns. Integrate with SIEM or observability platform.

name: LLM without output filtering
description: An LLM or model component does not have output filtering enabled, allowing potentially harmful, biased, or sensitive content to reach users.
recommendation: Deploy output filtering on all LLM components. Use guardrails, content safety classifiers, or moderation layers to filter harmful and sensitive content from outputs.
